```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has direct evidence that a solo builder can get paid for this exact product. The seed company dashp is cited at about $100k ARR, D2DHQ publishes $149-$499/mo plus a $500 onboarding fee, and an indie builder charges $20-$125/mo. That shows a real buyer with a real budget. Idea B has no comparable evidence that a new entrant has won paying support teams.",
    "In Idea A the payer is the pest control owner or sales-ops manager, a clear B2B buyer who controls the CRM and payroll access the product needs. In Idea B the brief itself admits the paying segment is uncertain. Its open question asks whether the real payer is a B2B support team or an unpaid family caregiver.",
    "Idea B's core feature has a price floor of zero. Microsoft Quick Assist ships free on Windows 10/11, and JoinByKey is free. Meanwhile, paid incumbents compete on SOC 2, HIPAA, SSO and CRM integrations, which one person cannot credibly match within 90 days.",
    "Idea A's demand evidence is concrete and money-linked: a litigated $217,494.60 commission dispute and a complaint about unresolved commission shortfalls. Idea B's demand quotes come from people helping elderly parents, not from support teams with budget.",
    "Idea A's main risk is serious but bounded. dashp reports about 5 months of in-person trust-building per closed deal and an ICP of only 'hundreds' of companies, which threatens the 90-day target. The low-priced indie competitor ($20/mo tier) suggests smaller teams may buy faster, but this is inference, not evidence. Idea B's main risk, that the payer may not exist at a price above free, is more fundamental."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence comes entirely from individual consumers helping elderly relatives: two posts on an Apple Support Community thread and an r/it thread about 'older parents.' None of it comes from a support team manager or CX lead, who is the stated payer. So the brief offers no direct evidence that its target buyer wants or would pay for the product. The quoted 41%/47% resolution gains are vendor marketing claims with no specific source link.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. A wins on evidence of willingness to pay and on payer clarity. Still, the brief's own source says closing a deal takes about 5 months, which directly conflicts with the 90-day paying-customer goal. A's demand quotes also come from reps and litigants rather than the owners who would pay. If a first sale cannot be compressed to a few weeks with small teams, A could miss the 90-day window too."
}
```
